name: OX Quiz Widget
description: A mobile-friendly educational O/X quiz interface that presents one question at a time, gives immediate answer feedback with explanations, and tracks progress.

requirement.summary: Build an O/X quiz widget for an educational mobile app. It shows one question at a time and lets the user pick O or X. After each choice it reveals whether the answer was correct and explains why. It also shows progress and lets the user retry the quiz, with a responsive layout, transition animations, and keyboard accessibility.
details: Display a list of O/X quiz questions one at a time, starting from the first question
Provide two answer buttons, O and X, for the user to select an answer to the current question
After selection, lock the answer buttons and reveal whether the user's answer is correct along with the correct answer and an explanation
Allow the user to advance to the next question after viewing feedback
Display progress as both text (e.g., '3/10 문제 완료') and a visual progress bar
Upon completing all questions, show a completion state with the final score (number of correct answers out of total)
Provide a retry ('다시 풀기') function that resets all state and restarts the quiz from the first question
Component structure: QuizContainer (overall quiz layout and state owner)
Component structure: QuestionCard (displays the current question text and question number)
Component structure: AnswerButtons (O/X selection buttons with disabled state after answering)
Component structure: ProgressBar (visual and textual progress indicator)
Component structure: ResultDisplay (correct/incorrect feedback with explanation)
Manage state for the current question index, the user's answers, whether each answer is correct, and quiz completion status
Accept quiz data as props (array of questions with id, question text, correct answer 'O' | 'X', and explanation), with built-in sample data as fallback
Responsive design optimized for mobile and tablet viewports
Include smooth transition animations when switching questions and revealing feedback, using Tailwind transition/animation utilities
Keyboard navigation support: Tab focus order, visible focus rings, Enter/Space to activate buttons, and optional shortcut keys (O/X or left/right arrows) for answering and Enter for next question
Accessibility: use semantic buttons, aria-labels for O/X buttons, aria-live region for result feedback, and progressbar role with aria-valuenow/aria-valuemax
Color scheme: green for correct answers, red for incorrect answers, gray for neutral/unselected states
Use the system default font stack (Tailwind font-sans)
Style exclusively with Tailwind CSS utility classes, with no custom CSS files or inline style objects
